tex_content.html: \begin{exercise} \end{exercise}1. ch10:10-19↗ prob:transverse-jacobi-field Suppose $P$ is an embedded submanifold in a Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$. A point $q \in M$ is said to be a focal point of $P$ if it is a critical value of the normal exponential map $E: \varepsilon _p \to M$ (see p. 133). Show that $q$ is a focal point of $P$ if and only if there exist a geodesic segment $\gamma : [0,b] \to M$ that starts normal to $P$ and ends at $q$ and a nontrivial Jacobi field $J \in \mathcal{J}(\gamma )$ that is transverse to $P$ in the sense defined in Problem 10-14 and satisfies $J(b) = 0$. (If this is the case, we say that $q$ is a focal point of $P$ along $\gamma $.) \end{exercise}
